Picked up a handful of new ones last week (9/7).

Glitterbomb #1 - Story of a 40ish actress trying to land roles as she has become too age for the entertainment industry. She gets possessed and/or inherits the ability to destroy those who treat her like crap. She seems to go into a trance when she defends herself, so not sure if she is going to have to learn to control her powers, or if an evil force has taken control of her body. The writing is really good, capturing what I imagine being in the leads position is like.

Rise of the Black Flame #1 - Daughters are being kidnapped from cities in Siam, and once two British(?) girls disappear with clues left behind, an investigation begins that takes two detectives outside of their jurisdiction to find a cult. I really like the artwork, and the story shows some brief glimpses of how great this could be in the next few books. This first issue is rather boring, but does the job as a setup for the world. Those panels every few pages that show what is possible are a great tease.

X-Files Origins #1 - Half the book follows Fox Mulder as a young teenager, and when you flip it and read from the opposite direction you get to read about Scully as a teenager. Orange Box Trailer (The first game on my steam account, what was yours?)

Half-Life 2. I got the silver edition, with Half-Life and Counter-Strike Source, but they were a separate installation code that I didn't redeem until a few months later. Then I didn't use Steam again for four years. After that...I broke the big 1k at the end of last year, so yeah

The first game on my Steam account was either Magic the Gathering: Duels of the Planeswalkers 2011 or realMyst. Both were bought in summer 2011 since I knew that Skyrim would require Steam that fall. I originally intended Steam only for games that required it and to minimize its use, but 400 games and 4 winter sales later Steam is my main source of gaming these days.

In general, I still dislike Steam's large market share in PC gaming (which is why I actually support Origin, uPlay, and especially GOG as well), but Steam is far better than most of the DRM schemes that predate it. The crap surrounding Spore and SecureROM comes to mind.
